newsitem.title: UK: UK'S Energy Group pretax profit up 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK'S Energy Group pretax profit up 16 pct.

text.p: UK'S Energy Group, due for demerger from the Hanson Plc in February, 1997, on Wednesday reported a 16 percent rise in proforma pre-tax profit to 446 million stg, for the year to September 30, 1996.
Its turnover before special discount stood at 3.77 billion stg, Hanson said.
Its earning per share stood at 60.7 pence.
The group said it was paying taxes of 131 million stg and transferring balance profit of 315 million stg to invested capital.
Energy Group's network profit for its UK operations rose seven percent to 211 million stg while its power profits for the same region rose 63 percent to 83 million stg.
It said its coal sales in the United States rose nine percent to 163 million tonnes. A cost reduction programme saved the company 45 million stg, it added.
After the demerger, the Energy Group would constitute a diversified energy business with interests in coal, power and networks.
Its main operations would be Eastern Group, which covers electricity and gas groups in Great Britain; and Peabody, the largest private producer of coal in the world.
The net assets of Energy group stood at 1.7 billion stg with its book gearing at 80 percent, it said.
